newsitem.title: USA: AMR against giving/selling 23 Heathrow slots.
newsitem.headline: AMR against giving/selling 23 Heathrow slots.

text.p: Robert Crandall, chairman of American Airlines' parent AMR Corp, said on Wednesday the company was not going to give away or sell 23 daily roundtrip rights to London's crowded Heathrow airport.
"We are not going to sell or make available sufficient slots to provide 23 rotations," Crandall told journalists before giving testimony to a Senate aviation subcommittee.

Earlier on Wednesday, the General Accounting Office, Congress's investigative arm, outlined a proposal to give 23 Heathrow slots to the six U.S. airlines competing with American Airlines' and British Airways' proposed operating alliance.

"The GAO says there needs to be competition, that's fine. We've acknowledged that," Crandall said. But he added there was no need for the American-BA alliance partners to give away landing rights at Heathrow.
He suggested that other airlines such as UAL Corp's United Airlines and Northwest Airlines Corp should either make full use of existing Heathrow rights or those of their European partner airlines.
